Let N be the category’s real-item catalogue size, excluding padding. The paper defines α=k/(N−1), β=α[t(1−1/α)+1/α]=1−t+tα. For k=128, t=0.75: β=0.25+0.75·128/(N−1). Exact loss: ℓ=−[β log σ(s⁺)+Σⱼlog(1−σ(sⱼ⁻))]/129. Thus β multiplies the positive log-loss; it is not a BCE `pos_weight` of 1/β. The equivalent positive-logit transformation is γ(s)=−log(σ(s)^(−β)−1). t=0 gives BCE; t=1 supplies the paper’s full-calibration setting. [IJCAI paper](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf)

A direct, numerically stable PyTorch implementation avoids sigmoid, powers and γ entirely: `beta = 0.25 + 0.75*128/(N-1); p = pos_logits[valid].float(); n = neg_logits[valid].float(); loss = ((beta*F.softplus(-p) + F.softplus(n).sum(-1))/129).mean()`, with positive logits shaped B×L, negative logits B×L×128, and `valid` selecting nonpadding training positions. This is algebraically equivalent to the authors’ transformation without its clipping approximations. Reduction matches their implementation: average over 129 candidates, then average over valid sequence positions. Separately averaging positive and negative losses changes their relative weighting. [Official training implementation](https://github.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch/blob/main/train_gsasrec.py)

Excluding every observed training positive changes the sampling distribution, so the paper’s calibration guarantee does not transfer unchanged. Inference: k/(N−|Hᵤ|) describes sampling from the remaining pool, but substituting this denominator alone cannot recover full-catalogue calibration because excluded items have zero negative-sampling probability. Retaining the published α/β is a heuristic under that sampler. Reproducibility caveat: the official PyTorch sampler draws with replacement from all real items, without rejecting even the target. [Official sampler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch/main/dataset_utils.py)
